item.title: Actor Tatyana Ali is advocating for Black and Indigenous maternal health
item.description: Actor Tatyana Ali says her healing journey after a traumatic childbirth has inspired her advocacy for Black maternal health, including support for midwives, doulas and other birth workers.

item.title: Black women are more likely to experience pregnancy trauma and have their pain ignored
item.description: Black mothers in the U.S. are three times as likely to die from pregnancy-related causes than white women. Actress Tatyana Ali became an advocate after her own awful experience giving birth.

item.title: 'People are still afraid of those three letters': Fighting the stigma of HIV
item.description: That's a quote from former rugby star Gareth Thomas, who is HIV positive. At the International AIDS Conference in Rio this year, he spoke out about the isolation and discrimination tied to the virus.

item.title: As diseases loom, CDC's response to measles deaths stirs fears about agency's reliability
item.description: The worst U.S. measles outbreak in decades is growing and flu season is imminent. Experts are fretting about federal health data reliability after the CDC questioned two Pennsylvania measles deaths.

item.description: Dr. Rupa Narra is a U.S. pediatrician who arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo to help care for stricken children. Nothing could have prepared her for what she'd face.
